headlines: BitMine Stock Falls to Key Support as Ethereum Crash Tests Tom Lee's Bull Run Thesis (Benzinga, Nov 22)
Why Is Bitmine Immersion Stock Falling on Friday? (Benzinga, Nov 20)
BitMine Hits 6M ETH Holdings but BMNR Drops 5% (Benzinga, Nov 16)
gappers.catalyst_detail: BitMine Immersion is an Ethereum treasury vehicle - its equity is a levered proxy on ETH, built around Tom Lee's thesis. It crossed 6.08M ETH holdings on Nov 16 and the stock fell 5% on the announcement, which tells you the accumulation story has stopped being a bid. Friday it dropped 13.87% to $12.98, a fresh 252-day low, as Bitcoin broke below $60,000 and Ethereum sold off hard. There is no BitMine-specific news today: the only Nov 23 item on its news feed is a generic crypto-market recap. The +9.4% gap is the equity bouncing with the Nasdaq, not with its own underlying asset.
gappers.why: Short-covering in the highest-beta corner of a market that closed Friday in correction. BMNR carries both equity-market beta and ETH beta; today only the equity leg is working. With the stock printing a 252-day low on Friday, the float was crowded short into a +3% Nasdaq futures gap, and that is the mechanism - a squeeze, not a re-rating.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline spike with a worse-than-usual foundation, because the thing it is supposed to track is not moving. BTC/USD is $61,230, +0.11%; ETH remains broken. A levered ETH proxy gapping +9.4% while ETH is flat is a divergence that historically closes toward the asset, not away from it. Sector read-through is to the crypto-treasury complex (Strategy hit a 52-week low Friday), which is the weakest group on the tape, not a leadership group. Premarket volume could not be measured (see notes), so there is no accumulation evidence to offset this.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Nothing structural changed - no ETH move, no company announcement, and the catalyst is a market-wide rate-expectation headline, so expect the gap to fade as soon as the index bid stops.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace: the account is 100% cash with 0 open positions and all 3 weekly trade slots free. The real cost is the slot itself, and BMNR is the worst name on this list to spend it on. It fails the 200-SMA long-bias filter by 30.0% and has no catalyst of its own. The stop geometry is disqualifying in a specific way: the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at $12.78, which is 0.96 ATR away AND two cents BELOW Friday's 252-day low of $12.80 - so the stop is parked exactly where the whole market can see it. A stop outside 1 ATR is $12.72 (-10.4%), already outside the 10% rule, and the matching 2:1 target of $17.16 (+20.8%) is 59.2% below the 252-day high. Cannot clear 2:1 at a legal stop. Not admissible.

gappers.catalyst: AI-infrastructure 'neocloud' bouncing after a -16.11% Friday; Nvidia's strong quarter lifted the group after hours Nov 20 and Bessent's anti-rate-hike comments extended it.
headlines: Nebius Shares Jump After Hours as Nvidia's Strong Quarterly Numbers Lift AI Infrastructure Stocks (Benzinga, Nov 20)
Nebius Group N.V. falls sharply by -16.11% to $81.31 on Friday (StockInvest, Nov 20)
Why Are Neocloud Stocks CoreWeave, IREN, and Nebius Rallying in Premarket Today, November 23? (TipRanks)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius is a GPU-cloud 'neocloud' and one of the most levered names to AI-capex sentiment. It fell 16.11% on Friday to $81.31 even though Nvidia had just posted strong quarterly numbers that lifted AI-infrastructure peers after hours - the group-wide de-rating overwhelmed the read-through. Today it gaps +8.52% alongside CoreWeave and IREN; TipRanks attributes the neocloud rally to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushing back against further Fed rate hikes on Sunday. That is a discount-rate story for long-duration growth equities, not a Nebius development. No Nebius-specific news has been published today.
gappers.why: Duration repricing. Neoclouds are the longest-duration, most capital-intensive AI assets on the tape, so they move hardest on any shift in rate expectations - down last week when hike odds rose, up today on a Treasury Secretary's pushback. The mechanism is entirely multiple, not earnings: a single official's weekend comment moved the group, and Nvidia's actual results on Nov 20 did not.
gappers.impact: Most likely to mean-revert of the five, because the volatility is extreme and the move is pure multiple. ATR(14) is 19.8% of price - NBIS routinely travels nearly 20% in a session, so an 8.5% gap is less than half a normal day's range and carries almost no informational content. The stock is 50.9% below its 200-SMA and 55.1% below its 50-SMA, i.e. not merely below trend but nowhere near it, and 72.9% off a $299.72 peak. Friday's close was only 10.6% above the 252-day low of $73.53. Read-through is to the whole neocloud complex (CRWV +7.04% here, IREN), which is the group that caused last week's correction - a bounce in the epicentre is the least durable kind.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst is one weekend remark about Fed policy, which is a sentiment input that can reverse at the next CPI or Fed speaker; nothing about Nebius's contracts, capacity or guidance changed.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (100% cash, 0 positions), so the cost is one of three weekly slots - and NBIS has the worst risk arithmetic on the entire list. The mandated 10% trailing stop at $79.42 is 0.51 ATR, barely half of one session's normal range: on a 19.8%-ATR stock that stop is not a risk control, it is a guaranteed exit on the first adverse open. To sit outside 1 ATR the stop must go to $70.81, which is -19.8% and roughly double the 10% rule's allowance, and the matching 2:1 target is $123.10 (+39.5%). Requiring a 40% advance to earn 2:1 on a name 50.9% below its 200-SMA is not a swing setup. Under the >0.75 correlation gate it would also block CRWV and the rest of the AI-infra block for the week. Not admissible on either the trend filter or the R:R minimum.

gappers.catalyst: Bouncing after a seventh straight down day (-11% Friday) triggered by a neutral analyst initiation at $83; CFO flagged a 'very strong uplift' in Electron pricing within nine months.
headlines: Rocket Lab Falls 11% As Weekly Slide Continues (TimothySykes, Nov 20)
Cramer believes Rocket Lab's recent share-price weakness has created an opportunity (TheStreet)
Rocket Lab shares plunged 12% after an analyst opened coverage with a neutral rating and an $83 price target
gappers.catalyst_detail: Rocket Lab fell about 11% on Friday to $45.42, its seventh consecutive daily decline, after a sell-side firm initiated coverage at neutral with an $83 price target - the same note gave AST SpaceMobile a $100 target, making it a relative-preference call within the space group rather than a verdict on the business. Pushing the other way, the CFO said Electron pricing should see a 'very strong uplift' within nine months, citing a record 54-launch Q3 book and tightening SpaceX rideshare capacity. Neutron remains the central growth catalyst and consensus sits near a $93 twelve-month target. Cramer publicly framed the weakness as an opportunity.
gappers.why: A seven-day sentiment unwind meeting a risk-on gap. Friday's decline was driven by an analyst preference shift, not an operating event; today's bounce is the market-wide relief rally giving holders a reason to stop selling. Underneath sits a real pricing-power mechanism: if capacity on the only cheaper alternative is tightening while RKLB's launch book is at a record, per-launch price is the margin lever - an operating fact rather than a target-price opinion.
gappers.impact: The most structurally sound move on today's list, though the gap itself is still beta. RKLB has the second-lowest ATR here at 11.0% of price and is the closest of the five to its own trend: 25.9% below its 50-SMA versus 29.5-55.1% for everything else. RSI(14) at 43.6 is the healthiest reading on the list - neither washed out nor extended - and Friday's close sat 20.8% above the $37.60 252-day low rather than on it, unlike BMNR. Read-through is to the launch/space complex, where RDW, LUNR and ASTS are all gapping 7.4-7.6% today; the fact that the entire group moves together in near-lockstep is itself the strongest evidence that today is the tide and not the thesis.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Neutron, a record 54-launch Q3 book and a CFO-guided Electron price uplift are structural changes, and launch/space infrastructure sits in Industrials - a favored sector in the early-cycle row of the rotation table - so this is the one name here worth a multi-day/week swing hold if it later clears the Confluence rule on a /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (100% cash, 0 positions). Because RKLB, RDW, LUNR and ASTS form one correlated space block, taking RKLB would consume effectively the whole space allocation for the week under the >0.75 correlation gate - and on thesis quality it is the right name to spend that slot on, ahead of RDW on franchise size and ahead of NBIS and BMNR outright. It still cannot be entered today. The 10% trailing stop at $44.01 is 0.91 ATR - the best ratio on this list but still inside one session's range, and it would have been hit on each of the last several days. A 1-ATR stop is $43.52 (-11.0%), fractionally outside the rule, and its 2:1 target of $59.66 (+22.0%) is the only target here that is genuinely reachable, sitting below the ~$93 consensus. The blocking failure is the 200-SMA long-bias filter - price is 37.1% below it - not the arithmetic. Watch, do not chase.

headlines: Redwire (NYSE:RDW) Stock Dropped to 'Sell' by Wall Street Zen (DefenseWorld, Nov 23)
Redwire Stock Rises After $15M Solar Array Contract with AscendArc (Benzinga)
Redwire Scores Fresh US Army Deal to Support High-Stakes Drone Training Missions (Benzinga)
Why Redwire (RDW) stock is nosediving (StockStory, Nov 5)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Redwire's Q3 on Nov 4 missed badly on revenue - roughly $109M against consensus near $126M - though the per-share loss was smaller than forecast; shares fell 19.4% that afternoon. Management held the 2026 revenue outlook at $450-500M and reported a record backlog near $620M. Since then the contract flow has been genuinely good: about $40M from NASA for Moon Base power generation (Nov 10), a $20M DARPA Otter testing contract, a follow-on U.S. Army order for Stalker drone support, and a $15M AscendArc order for ELSA solar-array wings, plus an insider purchase by CEO Peter Cannito. Working directly against today's gap, Wall Street Zen cut the stock from Hold to Sell dated Nov 23 - a same-day bearish action. Sell-side targets were cut broadly after the print: Piper Sandler to $8, Canaccord to $13, B. Riley to $14.
gappers.why: Group beta plus a cheap-optionality bid. RDW is the lowest-priced name in the space block, so it moves most per dollar of index risk appetite, and a record $620M backlog against a ~$6 share price gives bounce-chasers a story to point at. But the mechanism of today's move is not the contracts - those were announced between Nov 4 and Nov 20 and did not stop the stock from grinding to $5.65 - it is the same market-wide rate-expectation relief lifting the entire complex.
gappers.impact: Mixed, and the clearest case on the list of news cutting both ways on the same morning. The contract wins are real, repeat-customer, government-backed revenue, which is the most durable kind in this group - but the Q3 revenue miss was large, every major target was cut, and a fresh downgrade to Sell is dated today. The stock is 78.8% off its $26.64 high, 43.6% below its 200-SMA, and Friday's close of $5.65 sat only 15.8% above the $4.88 252-day low. Read-through is to the space block moving in lockstep (RKLB, LUNR, ASTS all +7.4-7.7%), confirming beta. With premarket volume unmeasurable there is no evidence of genuine accumulation behind the gap.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The contract wins are structural but are three weeks stale and already failed to hold the stock up; today's move is group beta against a same-day Sell downgrade, so treat it as a headline bounce rather than a re-rating.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (100% cash, 0 positions). Within the correlated space block the choice is RDW or RKLB, not both, and RKLB wins on every axis that matters: better trend position (-25.9% vs 50-SMA against RDW's -38.2%), lower volatility, healthier RSI, and a thesis not contradicted by a downgrade published this morning. Taking RDW would also forfeit the RKLB slot under the >0.75 correlation gate. The geometry fails regardless: the 10% stop at $5.47 is 0.82 ATR, inside one session's range, and a 1-ATR stop is $5.34 (-12.2%), outside the rule. The matching 2:1 target of $7.56 (+24.3%) is 71.6% below the 252-day high and below three of the four post-print analyst targets, so it is reachable on paper - but it cannot be paired with a legal stop. Not admissible.

headlines: NASA Awards Intuitive Machines Spot In $10 Billion Lunar Program (Benzinga, Nov 9)
Intuitive Machines (LUNR) Wins NASA CLPS 2 Contract, Shares Rise Premarket (GuruFocus)
Why Intuitive Machines Stock Went to the Moon on Monday (Motley Fool, Nov 9)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Intuitive Machines was selected in early November for NASA's CLPS 2 lunar delivery contract - a 10-year multiple-award framework with a $10B ceiling, extendable to $15B, shared among eight providers including Blue Origin, SpaceX and Firefly. The stock rose about 15% on the news around Nov 9. Its Q3 (Nov 12) disclosed roughly $450M of new awards plus Goonhilly acquired backlog, and its 10-Q lists a fifth NASA payload contract, IM-6, awarded March 2026 at an estimated $160.1M fixed-price. Despite all of that the shares have round-tripped the entire CLPS pop and more, closing Friday at $8.775 - the whole gain is gone, which analysts attribute to sector-wide multiple compression. B. Riley cut its target to $34 from $43 and KeyBanc to $30 from $38. No LUNR-specific news today.
gappers.why: Pure group beta on a name whose own good news has already been overwhelmed. The important mechanism here is what CLPS 2 actually is: an IDIQ framework that makes LUNR eligible to compete for missions, not a funded backlog - eight providers share the ceiling, so the headline $10B number overstates what accrues to any one of them. That is why a 15% pop faded completely, and why today's +7.46% - with no company news at all - should be read as the space complex moving together.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day spike on the weakest structural footing in the space block. LUNR is 81.2% off its $46.72 high, the worst drawdown on today's entire list, and 50.7% below its 200-SMA. Friday's close of $8.775 sat just 12.7% above the $7.79 252-day low. ATR(14) at 14.2% of price is the second-highest of the five. RSI(14) at 45.2 is the highest reading here, meaning LUNR is the least oversold of the group - it has the least mean-reversion fuel while carrying the most drawdown, which is the wrong combination. The read-through is unambiguous: RKLB, RDW and ASTS are all gapping within 0.2 points of the same percentage, which is the signature of an index bid, not five separate catalysts.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The CLPS 2 award is structural on paper but is an unfunded eight-way IDIQ framework that the market has already repriced to nothing over two weeks, and there is no fresh catalyst today - so this is a beta bounce with a short half-life.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (100% cash, 0 positions). LUNR is the weakest use of a weekly slot in the space block: it has the deepest drawdown, the least oversold RSI, and a flagship catalyst the market has already rejected over two full weeks of trading. Under the >0.75 correlation gate taking it would block RKLB, the one name here with a defensible multi-week thesis - which is the clearest opportunity cost on this list. The geometry also fails: the 10% stop at $8.49 is 0.70 ATR, well inside one session's range, and a 1-ATR stop is $8.09 (-14.2%), materially outside the 10% rule. The matching 2:1 target of $12.11 (+28.4%) is 74.1% below the 252-day high and still under both reduced analyst targets, but it cannot be paired with a legal stop. Not admissible.
